ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Suspicious Transaction Reporting Regulations, SOR/2002-317; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 462.31 et seq.; Civil Code of Québec, CQLR c. CCQ-1996, arts. 2236–2241; Legal Publicity Act, CQLR c. P-44.1; Act respecting the transparency of associations and enterprises, CQLR c. T-11.1; Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 21.1–21.5, as amended by Budget Implementation Act, 2023, S.C. 2023, c. 26.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Status Certificate of the Foreign Corporate General Partner or Parent Entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry or equivalent competent authority in the foreign entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the originating state's designated competent authority; consular legalization only if the state is not party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French or English Translation of the Foreign Entity's Charter, Articles or Partnership Agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator accredited in Quebec (OCCQ) based on the original authenticated document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of translator attestation and apostille of the underlying original document if required by the Registraire

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport and Proof of Address of Each Individual with Significant Control (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority and a public authority or bank issuing proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy of passport and apostille/legalization where the issuing jurisdiction requires it; address proof may bear sworn translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Source of Funds Confirmation for Contributions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank or credit union maintaining the contributor's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization depending on the bank's state of establishment; accompanied by sworn translation into French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney Authorizing Pre-Incorporation Filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or notarial authority in the jurisdiction of the constituent partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization for non-Hague states, and French sworn translation if executed outside Quebec

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, and authorised officers against United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions, Canadian sanctions regulations (Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; Criminal Code Part II.1 listed entities), OFAC SDN List, and other jurisdictional lists relevant to global EOR counterparties. PEP screening must follow FINTRAC guidance and FATF Recommendation 12, requiring Enhanced Due Diligence for foreign PEPs, inherent high-risk categories, and politically sensitive families. The compliance file must capture database report date, search logic, risk rating, and any false-positive resolution memo.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) — https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11), the proposed name must be presented in French. A non-French version may be registered only where a valid statutory exception exists (e.g., a recognized trademark composed exclusively of a non-French word or personal name). Names written in a non-Latin script must be transliterated into Latin characters in the declaration, and the transliteration must be cross-referenced in the authenticated apostille bundle.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Co-operative (unless the entity possesses valid cooperative status)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The applicant may file a revised name reservation with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec after a rejection, addressing the cited grounds and submitting a distinctiveness explanation. Where the refusal is based on a statutory prohibition or an identified conflicting name, the applicant may submit a written administrative reconsideration within 30 days of the notification, attaching evidence of prior rights and French-language compliance. If the Registraire upholds the refusal, a judicial application for review may be brought before the Cour du Québec under the Code of Civil Procedure; alternatively, the applicant may obtain a new 90-day reservation using a materially different name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A real, physical street address in Quebec is mandatory as the limited partnership's statutory domicile for service of process and registrar correspondence; a virtual mailbox-only arrangement is not acceptable for the registered office. For the EOR/staffing agency, the CNESST licence holder must maintain a demonstrable administrative establishment where employee records are located; a managed sublease or registered agent's professional suite with staffed reception may satisfy this only if administrative substance is genuinely maintained in Quebec.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 25% risk of a regulatory site inspection within the first 18 months of licensing. The risk rises above 40% where payroll complaints, corrected T4 issues, or UBO/sanctions screening flags are reported to FINTRAC or the CNESST. Stage-1 corporate registration alone is unlikely to trigger an on-site inspection.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Legal Publicity Act

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the Quebec Declaration of Limited Partnership (Déclaration de société en commandite)
Notarization, Hague Apostille, and consular legalization bundle for foreign corporate documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Professional per-document fee plus statutory authentication tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Compulsory French-language legal review and certified translation of governing documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator member of the OCCQ
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per source page, subject to OCCQ schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC UBO, PEP, OFAC, UN, and Canadian sanctions screening database research and compliance memo
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance data provider and legal counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Subscription per-report fee plus fixed counsel due diligence fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and corporate agent service for statutory domicile in Quebec (first 12 months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec-licensed corporate service provider or registered agent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Employment agency / EOR licence pre-application compliance assessment and CNESST permit fee (estimated)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail) and legal counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory permit fee plus pre-application advisory retainer

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec, RLRQ c. CCQ-1991, Articles 2236-2262 (Limited Partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, RLRQ c. P-44.1, ss. 2, 6, 17-27
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), enterprise register section, Quebec Government
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Statement of Registration) of the société en commandite / limited partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Quebec limited partnership; contributions are fixed exclusively by the partnership agreement and no capital need be advanced or escrowed at filing unless the agreement stipulates otherwise
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner approves and adopts the Limited Partnership Agreement dated ______ (the 'Partnership') validly constituted under Articles 2236 et seq. of the Civil Code of Quebec. RESOLVED, that the General Partner subscribes for its general partner units and records each limited partner's capital contribution as set out in Schedule A, no contribution being required to be paid or escrowed at formation. RESOLVED, that the registered office (siège social) shall be situated at [Montreal address], Province of Quebec, and that the Registraire des entreprises du Québec is directed to file the Partnership's Declaration of Registration. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and [Name] is appointed Compliance Officer of the General Partner, each authorized to execute all registrations, payroll accounts, and banking documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online portal — Recherche de nom
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search against the REQ enterprise register, submit a name reservation request identifying the partnership legal form ('société en commandite') and a descriptive statement of EOR/payroll services; complete the online form, pay the CAD$32 name-reservation fee, and obtain the Name Reservation Certificate before filing the registration declaration.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged as confusingly similar, submit a new application with alternative distinctive elements or file a consent letter from the prior name holder; any rejection notice may be answered within 15 days via REQ's online amendment process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil-law notary or corporate counsel in the Province of Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and sign the limited partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite) identifying the general partner (commnadité), limited partners (commanditaires), capital schedules, profit-sharing ratios, restrictions on limited partner management, and audit rights; have all partners execute the agreement, with execution witnessed before a notary when a corporate general partner is acting; retain the original for inspection by REQ or banks upon request.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ or a bank queries the agreement, amend by unanimous written consent of partners and execute a supplementary agreement; then file a declaration of modification (déclaration modificative) where the register requires updated information.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the enterprise with the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Immatriculation d'une société en commandite
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Declaration of Registration using REQ's secure 'Accès clients' portal or paper form; provide the exact registered-office address in Quebec, legal form, general partner's name and domicile, the declared business activities, and the date of the partnership agreement; pay the CAD$55 first-section registration fee plus CAD$20 per additional section.
required_dossiers: General partner's corporate resolution appointing signatories
Registered office address proof (lease or utility bill)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a 'refusal to immatriculer' notice, cure within 30 days by correcting the declaration, producing a compliant address in Quebec, and reconciling the general partner's designation; any refusal is appealable to the Court of Québec after exhausting REQ's internal rectification process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax account registration with Revenu Québec and CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec — AccèsD Affaires; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the REQ registration attestation, open a Quebec enterprise file with Revenu Québec and simultaneously register with the CRA for a federal Business Number (BN); enroll for GST/HST, Quebec QST, payroll source deductions (employee income tax, CPP/QPP, QPIP), and register the entity with CNESST as an employer; provide the LP partnership Social Insurance-compliant identification and the general partner's tax identifiers.
required_dossiers: General partner's social insurance / business number
Bank confirmation of partnership bank account
List of directors and officers for beneficial ownership reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax account application is rejected or incomplete, resubmit the corrected application within 30 days; request a ministerial waiver of interest in cases of CRA or Revenu Québec administrative delay and maintain a written chronology of filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST), Direction générale du travail
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the licence application under Quebec's Act respecting labour placement agencies and personnel recruitment agencies (RLRQ c. A-12.0001); file the REQ registration slip, attest that the enterprise will not charge fees to workers, present a compliant business plan for cross-border EOR payroll, and pay the prescribed licence fee; secure mandatory liability insurance or a financial guarantee before the licence is issued.
required_dossiers: Proof of head office and Quebec nominated address
Criminal record check of the general partner and directors
Business plan and EOR client services description
Certificate of liability insurance or financial guarantee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence application is refused or queried, supply the missing information within 30 days; an adverse licence decision may be contested before the Tribunal administratif du travail (TAT) within 60 days, with continued lawful operation pending first instance only if a prior licence existed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) acting under the Minister of Labour, with co-administration by the Quebec Ministry of Employment for foreign worker placement
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence d'agence de placement de personnel (Personnel Placement Agency Licence) covering temporary and permanent EOR placement, contractor payroll, and cross-border employment administration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II – Registration only; office-based administrative use qualifies for ministerial registration without a full EIA, subject to municipal zoning confirmation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluent or atmospheric discharge is generated by an EOR staffing office; tenants must comply with municipal greywater and sanitary sewer bylaws (REA of Quebec municipalities), the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of products for e-waste, and MELCCFP standards for lighting, heating, and ventilation pollutants; high-latitude energy efficiency standards apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal occupancy permit (permis d'occupation) from the local borough; fire safety certificate issued by the local fire safety service demonstrating compliance with the Safety Code under the Règlement sur la sécurité incendie; CNESST workplace health and safety registration and display obligations; conformity certificate for landlord-required building capacity and emergency exits; elevator and accessibility inspection by the RBQ (Régie du bâtiment) where the leased premises contain mechanical lifts or public access areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), federal portal: My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html); Revenu Québec, provincial portal: clic Revenu (https://www.revenuquebec.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Deposit the Quebec limited partnership's declaration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) to obtain the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), naming the foreign general partner and appointing an attorney in Quebec. Step 2: Use CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1 to create the federal Business Number (BN) and open the required program accounts, including GST/HST (RT), payroll deductions (RP), and import/export (RM) where applicable. Step 3: Register with Revenu Québec under the same Quebec enterprise number for QST/TVQ and Quebec employer source deductions (QPIP, HSF, and provincial income tax withholdings). Step 4: Submit the partnership agreement, non-resident ownership declarations, and foreign tax residence certificates during registration. Step 5: Maintain ongoing filings through CRA and Revenu Québec portals, including T5013 information returns, GST/HST and QST returns, and payroll remittances.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification: Canada does not offer a US-style check-the-box election or a general hybrid-mismatch election for limited partnerships. A Quebec LP is mandatorily flow-through for income tax and is treated as a separate person for GST/HST/QST purposes. Limited partnership fiscal-period and partner-representative designations may be filed under applicable tax acts, but these do not alter entity-level classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) at the federal level, plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) at the provincial level.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 in taxable supplies made in Canada, including zero-rated supplies, over the current calendar quarter or the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters for GST/HST; the same C$30,000 threshold applies for QST. A Quebec LP engaged in employer-of-record and payroll services should nevertheless register promptly because it is making taxable supplies and must remit payroll source deductions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or tax-authority API authorization applies in Canada or Quebec. GST/HST and QST invoices must contain the supplier's registration number, transaction date, description, consideration, tax rates, and tax amounts. Invoices issued in Quebec must generally be in French unless the parties otherwise agree. Registered persons must file periodic returns electronically through CRA GST/HST NETFILE and Revenu Québec's secure transmission portal; no digital fiscal seal is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Excise Tax Act, a supply of a service to a non-resident person is zero-rated where the service is not rendered to an individual while that individual is in Canada, is not in relation to real property situated in Canada, and is not in relation to tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed. Global EOR and cross-border contractor payroll administration supplied by the Quebec LP to a foreign end-client generally falls within this exported-services rule if the recipient is a non-resident person not registered for GST/HST and the service is not rendered to an individual present in Canada or tied to Canadian real or tangible property. QST applies an equivalent zero-rating rule for services supplied to non-residents. The LP must obtain and retain contemporaneous evidence of the recipient's non-resident status and the place of supply to support the 0% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Signed global EOR/contractor payroll services agreement citing the non-resident recipient and the place of supply.
Invoice issued under GST/HST/QST rules showing the client's foreign address and the 0% rate applied.
Non-resident status evidence, such as foreign corporate register extract, foreign tax identification number, or certificate of residence.
CBSA Export Declaration (Form B13A) and bill of lading or air waybill where any physical goods are bundled with the services.
Bank remittance or inward-remittance certificate demonstrating receipt of cross-border payment within the FX repatriation period.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If export zero-rating is disallowed, CRA and Revenu Québec will reassess the supply at the standard GST and QST rates, add statutory interest, and claw back input tax credits claimed on costs attributable to that supply. Gross negligence or false statement penalties under the Excise Tax Act and Quebec's QST regime are generally the greater of C$100 and 25% of the tax understated; deliberate fraud may attract criminal prosecution. Failure to maintain the required non-resident and foreign-remittance documentation within the 180-day period will trigger heightened audit scrutiny and retrospective reassessments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BOC) – the central monetary authority; however, Canada maintains no separate foreign-exchange control agency. Currency policy and exchange-control administration fall under the Minister of Finance and the Department of Finance Act, with anti-money laundering oversight by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both capital and current accounts under the Bank of Canada Act, Currency Act, and Commercial Companies policy. There are no exchange controls, quotas, or licensing requirements for cross-border transfers. Profit remittances for non-resident limited partners are free of Forex authority approval, subject only to corporate tax obligations (Quebec CRA) and FINTRAC reporting on international EFTs of CAD 10,000 or above.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender or mandatory conversion rules apply to export proceeds in Canada (and none apply to an EOR service provider). Exporters may hold foreign currency indefinitely. The only legislative relevance is the PCMLTFA, which requires reporting of cross-border transfers of CAD 10,000 or more; it does not impose any timing or conversion mandate.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium. Canadian law under PCMLTFA requires every money-services business (MSB) providing foreign-exchange dealing or remittance services to register with FINTRAC and, for operations in Quebec, hold a licence from the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) under the Money-Services Businesses Act (Quebec). Offshore EMIs without such registrations cannot lawfully open settlement accounts in Canada. The platform 'Wise' is registered as an MSB and holds AMF licensing (or operates under the federal registration), so it can serve as a secondary payment rail for small cross-border contractor disbursements; however, Wise is not a chartered foreign bank and cannot hold corporate deposits or provide payroll tax remittance services. A Schedule I bank account remains mandatory for statutory deductions, payroll taxes, and capital-bearing escrow functions. Legal constraints also include the prohibition on treating EMI balances as collateral.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are not required to appear physically in Canada for bank onboarding, provided that a compliant video-conference identity verification (including liveness detection and notarized passport copies) is completed. In practice, Canada's Big Six banks each allow fully remote onboarding for a Quebec LP when: (a) the general partner is a Canadian resident corporation or (b) non-resident partners are covered by a Canadian attorney-in-fact registered under the Quebec Company Records. Remote opening mandates submission of the Declaration of Registration (Registraire des entreprises – REQ) and the partnership's 3032 certificate. A minority of banks (e.g., some credit unions) still require an in-person bank interview with an authorized signatory at a local branch, but this is not a statutory requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partner (individual or corporate) with no Canadian nexus appearing as beneficial owner of >25% of the LP
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submission of a corroborated corporate structure chart covering ultimate human beneficial owners; declaration of source of wealth and source of funds; audited financial statements of the parent entity; and a Quebec business purpose letter explaining the EOR service scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partnership control ambiguity (e.g., separate general partner vs. limited partner authority)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the certified partnership agreement, the REQ registration extract naming the general partner, and a power-of-attorney document confirming the signatory’s authority; also include a current Certificate of Statutory Compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume payroll wires to international contractors without supporting contracts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compile an EOR services client contract, per-contractor service agreements, digital worker onboarding records, and payroll registers with corresponding tax filings (Relevé 1 / T4 summaries) to establish a genuine business flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injections from higher-risk jurisdictions (e.g., non-OECD states)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a legal opinion letter from a licensed Canadian counsel attesting to the legitimacy of the investment; origin of funds statement from the foreign partner; sanctions screening run against OSFI and FINTRAC lists; and evidence of tax registration in the source state.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route all inbound partner capital via SWIFT MT103 with a narrative strictly stating 'Capital contribution for LP operational funding – CAD conversion for payroll services'. The remitter must include the LP's Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and the purpose code ‘G - Business and other operating expenses’ (or equivalent per the bank's required coding). Banks will auto-register the EFT form with FINTRAC when the amount is >= CAD 10,000. The receiving account must be a dedicated CAD capital-injection account to avoid commingling; a separate operating payroll account should be used for daily disbursements. For contributions in USD/EUR, instruct the executing bank to convert at the interbank spot rate and provide a mirror confirmation before final booking.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic payroll (Quebec employees) is settled via Payments Canada’s LVTS/ACSS using direct-deposit EFTs (credit payments) through the ODBC interface or the bank's invoice-based bulk payment portal. International contractor payments use SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for cover) cleared through the correspondent network; alternatively, use a licensed MSB rail such as Wise for low-value disbursements to avoid high wire fees. Settlement under commercial letters of credit (LC) is not standard for payroll, but for any purchase of benefits administration services, an LC may be opened on the bank's trade-desk using the documentary collection (DP/DA) route. All outbound transfers must be reported per PCMLTFA thresholds, and beneficiary name/passport elements must be included to satisfy enhanced due diligence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright and dated FX forward contracts (spot-deferred) for CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP executed with a Schedule I bank or an approved OSFI-regulated swap dealer

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts for convertibility-restricted pairs (e.g., CAD/CNY) settled in USD via clearing-house mechanisms, permissible because CAD is not conventionally prohibited but used only for currency pairs without active swap rates
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to convert USD capital contributions into CAD liabilities, matching EOR payroll cashflows and eliminating mark-to-market volatility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual updating declaration and annual registration fee for the Quebec limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the prescribed annual updating period, generally the six-month period following the partnership's fiscal year-end; confirm the exact period in the REQ record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or missing annual updating obligations may result in administrative penalties, loss of good standing, and ex officio cancellation after the applicable non-compliance period, generally following two consecutive omitted annual declarations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal year-end where the partnership is required to file under the Income Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties may apply, with additional penalties for failure to provide required partner information; repeated non-compliance may trigger audit or enforcement action

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec partnership information return (Form TP-600-V), where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within five months after the partnership's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, interest, and partner-assessment consequences may apply; Revenu Québec may issue compliance requests or reassess the partnership and its partners

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general Quebec statutory independent-audit requirement applies solely because the entity is a limited partnership. An audit may be required by the partnership agreement, lender, investor, grantor, or applicable tax or regulatory rule. Payroll and staffing licensing requirements should be assessed separately.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian accounting standards for private enterprises (ASPE) are generally applicable for private partnership financial reporting; IFRS may be used where adopted or contractually required. Quebec and Canadian tax filings must follow applicable tax legislation and prescribed forms.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The partnership must maintain current information on partners, controlling persons, and beneficial owners and update the REQ when reportable information changes. The annual updating declaration must confirm or update the enterprise's registry information. Changes should be filed within the applicable statutory period, generally 30 days after the change; verify current REQ beneficial-ownership exemptions and disclosure rules.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Current register of general and limited partners, including contribution and interest records
Register of beneficial owners and controlling persons, with supporting identification records
Register of partnership resolutions and material decisions
Accounting records, financial statements, tax filings, and supporting documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 600-1,800 per year, approximately USD 430-1,300, for a Quebec registered office and local administrative or filing agent, depending on service scope
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500-12,000 for an independent review or audit of a small limited partnership; a full audit may exceed this range depending on payroll volume, partner count, cross-border activity, and control complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal 15% (non-CCPC general corporate rate) + Quebec 11.5% general provincial corporate rate, combined statutory headline 26.5%; an LP is fiscally transparent, so the headline rate tax is borne by corporate or individual partners at their own rates.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction reducing the federal rate to 9% on active business income up to CA$500,000 (available to Canadian-controlled private corporation partners, not to the LP itself); SR&ED investment tax credits (federal 15%–35% refundable); Quebec R&D tax credits (35% for large corporations, 30% for SMEs), accelerated capital cost allowance for eligible payroll/IT equipment, and Quebec's 10-day tax holiday for foreign specialists (within specified limits).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 – Statement of Partnership Income (CRA 'T5013' e-file via GST/HST NETFILE-approved software or Represent a Client portal); Quebec: TP-601 (Déclaration de renseignements des sociétés de personnes) filed electronically via Revenu Québec's EDT (Transmission électronique des déclarations) service.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Both T5013 and TP-601 are due no later than five months after the end of the LP's fiscal year (typically March 31 for a December 31 year-end LP, i.e., May 31); corporate partners must file their T2/TP-600 returns within six months of their own fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from the EOR services rendered (payroll administration and employer-of-record fees) before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only revenue attributable to the Canadian/Quebec permanent establishment; intercompany charges from the global EOR platform must be excluded or separately reported in the reconciliation schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 08 – Gross cost of goods sold / cost of payroll services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of providing EOR services, including salaries of employees placed under the employer-of-record arrangement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Salaries of Canadian-resident employees are deductible only if remitted through qualified Quebec payroll accounts (QPP, QPIP, EI, HSF); no deduction is allowed for non-resident payroll unless the employee is registered with CRA as a Canadian-reportable employee.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net active business income from the LP's EOR operations after all deductible expenses, including management fees, platform licensing fees and technology costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductibility of platform fees paid to foreign affiliates requires compliance with ITA s.247 (transfer pricing) and, for Quebec, the restriction on expenses such as management fees paid to non-residents (Quebec Taxation Act).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sale of capital assets held by the LP (if any).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must report a capital gains allocation only where the asset is 'taxable Canadian property' subject to Part I tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part III – Allocation schedule (T5013 partner allocation / TP-601 RL-15 slips)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's share of income/loss, contribution schedule, and partnership percentage; Quebec RL-15 (Revenus d'une société de personnes) must be issued to each partner resident in Quebec.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident corporate partner, the LP must attach the name, address, treaty-residence identifier and the agreed allocation percentage; the LP must not withhold Part XIII on business-income allocations but must be prepared to apply ITA s.226(1) if CRA issues a demand for the non-resident partner's unpaid Part I tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: CRA: late filing penalty under ITA s.162(7) is CA$25/day (minimum CA$100, maximum CA$2,500), plus a s.162(7.1) penalty of CA$100 per partner per month (maximum 24 months) for failing to file T5013 information; Revenu Québec: daily penalties up to CA$2,500 plus interest at the prescribed rate, and 50% gross-negligence penalties for false or misleading statements.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under ITA Part XIII (s.212(2)) on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation; an LP itself is a flow-through and its profit distributions to non-resident partners are not 'dividends' — such active business income is taxable under Part I on the non-resident partner, subject to the DTA permanent-establishment rule.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA, the non-resident corporate partner must (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority (e.g., IRS Form 6166 for a US partner); (2) complete and file CRA Form NR301 (Application for a Reduction in the Amount of Non-Resident Tax Withheld) before payment; (3) maintain contemporaneous records of the treaty entitlement; and (4) where a Canadian tax return is required, file Form NR7 series with the CRA within two years of the end of the taxation year to obtain refund relief. For business profits (no Canadian PE), the LP should record the T5013 allocation as Canadian-source business income and the partner claims treaty exemption by filing a Part I return through an appointed representative; Quebec applies the same treaty lines through the tax-collection agreement with CRA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate: 25% for interest and royalties paid to non-resident licensors/lenders. Under the Canada–US Treaty: interest 0% (exempt) for arm's-length and related-party interest where the beneficial owner is a US resident; royalties 0% for industrial/software royalties under Article XII of the Treaty. Under Part XIII service fees and management fees are generally not subject to WHT (taxed as business income through the PE filter).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation is mandatory (ITA s.247(4)) where the LP's aggregate cross-border transactions with non-residents exceed CA$1,000,000 per year; CRA administrative guidance TP-2023-07 requires a Local File where the Canadian entity's gross revenue exceeds CA$10,000,000 and a Master File where the MNE group's consolidated group revenue exceeds CA$1,000,000,000. Country-by-country reporting (CbCR) applies to ultimate parents with consolidated group revenue of EUR 750,000,000 (approximately CA$1.1 billion).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP – Comparable Uncontrolled Price (most appropriate for benchmarked EOR per-employee pricing)
Resale Price Method (for distribution/pass-through payroll fee structures)
Cost Plus Method (for intercompany payroll administration services rendered to the global platform)
Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) (preferred by CRA for routine EOR payroll processing using operating margin indicators)
Profit Split Method (where the LP and the global platform jointly own intangibles such as the EOR platform software)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); however, the federal GAAR (ITA s.245), the Quebec GAAR (Quebec Taxation Act ss.1079.1–1079.11), the doctrine of 'place of effective management' and the OECD BEPS Action 5 minimum standard require genuine commercial substance. A Quebec LP acting as global EOR must maintain physical premises, full-time payroll operations staff, actual client contracts, payroll remittance records (federal and Quebec payroll accounts), and substantive decision-making in Quebec; a passive 'shell LP' holding only the EOR platform license will be recharacterized, leading to denial of the LP flow-through status and 50% gross-negligence penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Unremitted Payroll Source Deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Collecting income tax, QPP, QPIP and EI premiums from global employees but failing to remit to CRA/Revenu Québec on PD7A/TPZ due dates, or wilfully misclassifying employees as independent contractors to avoid payroll obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA: 10% late-remittance penalty plus daily interest; 50% gross-negligence penalty (ITA s.163(2)) on unreported amounts; criminal fines on summary conviction of 50%–200% of the evaded tax (ITA s.239) and up to 5 years' imprisonment upon indictment; Quebec TAA: additional 50% penalty and criminal fines up to CA$575,000 for directors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable under ITA s.227.1 and Quebec TAA s.32 for unremitted source deductions without proof of fault; the due-diligence defence (exercising reasonable care based on delegated financial specialists) is narrow; a personal restitution order, asset freezing, exclusion from the CRA/Revenu Québec top-debtor programme, and judicial restrictions on leaving Canada for outstanding tax debts exceeding CA$7,500 are available.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company – Sham LP and Artificial Allocation of Profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Quebec LP solely to register a DTA-accessible permanent establishment or to shift profits from the foreign parent to a Quebec head office with no personnel, no payroll contracts and no client onboarding activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization under the sham doctrine and GAAR with a 50% gross-negligence penalty on re-assessed income (ITA s.163(2)); denial of the LP's flow-through status; transfer-pricing adjustments under ITA s.247(2) with a 10% adjustment penalty on the lesser of 10% of gross revenue and CA$5,000,000; Revenu Québec impositions under the Quebec GAAR mirroring the federal rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate-general-partner directors face joint liability for the re-assessed partnership tax and a court-ordered civil restitution of diverted profits; criminal counselling of false statements ('fraud on CRA') opens the directors to indictment under ITA s.239 and to a travel-restriction order pending the criminal trial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / FINTRAC Compliance Failure – Unregistered Money Services Business
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an unregistered money-services/foreign-remittance rail (e.g., wrapping Wise/B2B payment APIs) that transfers funds for international contractors without registering as an MSB or obtaining a Canadian money-services-business licence under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to register a money-services business with FINTRAC is an offence punishable on summary conviction by a fine up to CA$500,000 and 2 years' imprisonment, or on indictment by a fine up to CA$1,000,000 and 5 years' imprisonment for the EOR entity; each failure to send an electronic funds-transfer report carries administrative monetary penalties up to CA$10,000 per violation for compliance failures and CA$500,000 for deliberate AML violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly authorize an unregistered money-transfer service are personally liable for the corporate fines, may face criminal prosecution (maximum fine CA$1,000,000 and 5 years' imprisonment), and may be made subject to a restraint order freezing personal and corporate assets for the duration of the FINTRAC/RCMP investigation.
